---
title: DEF Tools
---

`def-tools` parses and queries DEF (Design Exchange Format) designs through a
Rust backend. DEF coordinates come out in database units (DBU) as they appear
in the file. Plain `.def` and gzipped `.def.gz` inputs are both read. Cell LEF
parsing lives in `lef-tools`; the DEF backend links it for macro sizes, so the
Python packages stay independent.

## Install

```bash
cd def_tools
uv sync --dev
uv run def-tools --help
```

Or install it from the repository:

```bash
uv tool install "def-tools @ git+https://github.com/smprather/open-eda-file-tools.git#subdirectory=def_tools"
```

The test suite stores no design files. To try the commands, generate a small
synthetic design in a checkout:

```bash
cd def_tools
uv run python -m tests.gen.design_gen -o /tmp/design -n 500
```

That writes `design.lef`, `design.def.gz`, `design.sdc` and a `manifest.json`
of ground truth.

## Commands

### `def-tools instances`

Write placed instance bounding boxes as CSV. `--lef` may be repeated;
duplicate macro names resolve to the last definition and a warning lists them.
`--threads` bounds the rayon pool for component parsing.

```bash
uv run def-tools instances \
  --lef /tmp/design/design.lef --def /tmp/design/design.def.gz \
  --output instances.csv
```

Columns: `instance,macro,status,orient,llx,lly,urx,ury`.

### `def-tools net-shapes`

Write routed shape bounding boxes for one net and layer. Supply either a DEF
(`--def`) or a cache directory (`--cache-dir`). Path segments are emitted as
rectangular DBU bounding boxes using the DEF route width.

```bash
uv run def-tools net-shapes --def design.def.gz \
  --net VDD --layer met1 --output vdd_met1.csv
```

Columns:
`net,section,route_status,shape_type,layer,width,x1,y1,x2,y2,llx,lly,urx,ury`.

### `def-tools cache create`

Convert a DEF once into an indexed binary cache directory for repeated queries
on huge gzipped files:

```bash
uv run def-tools cache create --def design.def.gz --output design.ldefcache
```

The cache stores components, raw net records, a fixed-offset net record index,
a net-name index and parsed connectivity in separate files. A single-net query
therefore reads only the matching records, and clock queries skip DEF
tokenization.

### `def-tools clock-instances`

Extract clock roots from SDC `create_clock` / `create_generated_clock`
commands and walk DEF connectivity through clock cells. `--clock-cell-pattern`
is a substring matched against macro names and defaults to `clk`; repeat it to
add patterns.

```bash
uv run def-tools clock-instances --sdc design.sdc \
  --cache-dir design.ldefcache --output clocks.csv
```

Columns:
`clock,root_type,root_name,instance,macro,net,is_clock_cell`.

### `def-tools configure-io`

Benchmark storage targets and write a TOML config with filesystem type, free
space, ranked scratch directories, RAM directories and cache defaults. It uses
Flexible I/O Tester (`fio`) when available and valid, otherwise a built-in
sequential benchmark.

```bash
uv run def-tools configure-io \
  --target /scratch/$USER \
  --target /dev/shm \
  --output def-tools-io-config.toml
```

`--probe-mib` caps the benchmark file size per target and `--engine` selects
`auto`, `internal` or `fio`.

## Python API

```python
from def_tools import instance_bboxes

for bbox in instance_bboxes(["sky130.lib.lef"], "design.def.gz"):
    print(bbox.instance, bbox.llx, bbox.lly, bbox.urx, bbox.ury)
```

`instance_bboxes` multiplies each LEF macro's `SIZE` by the DEF's database
units per micron. A LEF that does not define a placed macro raises an error
naming the missing macro.

### Aligned table

`write_instance_table` writes the same rows as an aligned text table and
returns the row count. The native writer sizes the columns with a
components-only pass and then streams the rows:

```python
from def_tools import write_instance_table

write_instance_table(["sky130.lib.lef"], "design.def.gz", "instances.table")
```

`write_instance_bbox_csv` writes the same rows as CSV and returns the row
count; both writers stream without loading the design into memory.

`write_instance_parquet` writes zstd-compressed Parquet in row groups of
`batch_size` rows and returns `(rows, row_groups)`:

```python
from def_tools import write_instance_parquet

rows, groups = write_instance_parquet(
    ["sky130.lib.lef"], "design.def.gz", "instances.parquet", 131_072
)
```
